text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA
- Korea's Daewoo will soon appoint a head of the Warsaw-based Daewoo FSO plant to replace Jin Chul Suk, recently arrested in Korea, plant spokeswoman Krystyna Danilczyk said.

- It is impossible to extend the scope of the National Investment Fund (NFI) privatisation programme, though it could be complemented by similar regional or industrial funds, the treasury ministry's state secretary for privatisation Wieslaw Kaczmarek said.
- Poland's and Belgium's labour ministries and the EU committee for social and economic affairs held a conference in Warsaw on employee councils in multinational corporations.

- Poland's rail company PKP will have to modernise the wheel system of its rolling stock due to the forecast EU introduction of a mono-block wheel system in two years time. The modernisation will cost 450 million zlotys.
- Poland's housing developers underestimate the benefits of cooperation with banking institutions, financial sector representatives said at a conference on the housing industry.
- The Rzeszow-based Elektromontaz electrical engineering and construction firm has got the International Standards Organisation (ISO)-9001 quality certificate for its projects, products and services.
- BMB Promotions Ltd will start publishing Poland's first insurance monthly "Asekuracja & Re". The first issue will appear by Christmas, publisher Wieslaw Uzieblo said.
- Krakow-based Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy (BPH) opened 26 new branches in 1996, which increased their number to 145 outlets and made it Poland's third biggest banking chain.

- The Warsaw-based Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego (BGK) and the Fundusz Gornoslaski fund will cooperate in future investment consortia and facilitate credit guarantees for small and medium size firms, an agreement by the two firms said.
NOWA EUROPA
- The Elblag-based soft commodities exchange is nearing completion of its infrastructure modernisation programme worth three million zlotys, the exchange's managing company said.
- Listed stock prices on central European bourses are still low, Mercury Asset Management board director Stephen Cohen said.
- The listed Prochnik garment maker's annual net profit this year will exceed one million zlotys, Prochnik's president Adam Sasiadek said.
- The listed Bytom garment maker has issued two month commercial papers with five million zlotys nominal value.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- Poland's insurance guarantee fund has refunded 10 million zlotys in damages to people formerly insured by the bankrupt Gryf insurance firm, while the bankrupt Hestja insurance policy holders have been repaid 748,000 zlotys.
- Production of goods including asbestos will be banned in Poland as of January 1, 1997, the construction ministry said.
- The profitability of carp breeding has declined by 30 percent since 1994, the IRS inland fisheries' institute said.
ZYCIE
- Poland's banking climate is declining in December due to a 0.15 percent decrease in corporate sector credits compared with last month, a Pentor polling institute survey showed.

- Poland's economic ministers' committee (KERM) plans to create a soft commodities marketing agency (AMARS) in two years' time to promote the country's food products abroad. For its first five years the agency will be funded by the government and will later become a joint stock company.
PARKIET
- The Warsaw-based Kredyt Bank (KB) will acquire a share stake in a Russian bank operating in the Kalinigrad region, KB's president Stanislaw Pacuk said. He did not name the bank.
- The Szczecin-based Odra jeans maker will be privatised in th first half of 1997, the company said.
- The listed PPWK map maker's revenues in November were 1.7 million zlotys, a 35 percent growth compared with the same period last year.
